Yuri Diordatzia, eldest son of Natalia and Dmitry, was born on 18 Tammuz 5760 (21 July 2000) in the city of Kropyvnytskyi in Ukraine, the capital of Kirovohrad Oblast. He has a brother, Marko.

Yuri grew up in his hometown and studied for eleven years at the HBK school (the Kirovohrad College). He was a good student and active in the school's social life. From the age of thirteen he practiced weightlifting, took part in competitions and won them.

After finishing high school, Yuri was accepted to the Volodymyr Vynnychenko Central Ukrainian State University. He studied in the faculties of history and law, subjects he especially loved, and specialized in political science. At university, too, he was the driving spirit in his studies and social life, and he continued to take part in sports competitions. He competed in the Kirovohrad Oblast Open Weightlifting Championships, and he would say that for him taking part in competitions mattered more than the results, and that the prizes he won were a "bonus."

In 2019, Yuri immigrated to Israel alone in order to serve in the army. About a year and a half later he enlisted in the IDF as a lone soldier, and he served in the Navy.

He told his mother that he had met interesting people in the army. His fellow soldiers described him as sensitive and gentle, radiating light and joy, with a beautiful smile from ear to ear. "A good friend with a giant heart."

Corporal Yuri Diordatzia fell during his service on 4 Elul 5782 (31 August 2022). He was twenty-two years old. He was laid to rest in the Kropyvnytskyi-Rovenetska cemetery in Ukraine. He is survived by his parents and his brother.

After his death he was promoted to the rank of Sergeant.

His mother wrote: "Yuri was my soul and my wings. It is hard for me to find the words to express how much."
